chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Will the earth remain without an Imam?' He replied: 'If the earth were to remain without an Imam for a moment, it would cave into itself.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the earth if it is without an Imam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Abu Hamza al-Thumali asks Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) about the state of the earth during the Minor Occultation, receiving the profound response that the earth would 'sink' without an Imam. This highlights the Shia doctrine of *Hujjah* (Proof), where the Imam serves as the existential anchor (*Asas*) of the universe, maintaining cosmic order and preventing chaos. The metaphor of sinking underscores the metaphysical necessity of the Imam's presence for the stability of creation.
